title: skills(objectstack-data): the registerHook example says "in your plugin's onEnable()", but a kernel plugin has init/start, and onEnable is the app's config export
body:
repo:objectstack#2 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgV6i8jfWwSXjpWJrjA

Filing gate: ① (an out-of-scope finding of a dev report, escalated by the contract review) · Source: fleet (PR #38155, the card thread's report on #35324 and contract review 7234212662, section ③)

## What happens

`skills/objectstack-data/references/data-hooks.md` (Hook registration, method 2, `ctx.ql.registerHook()`) opens its example with the comment `// in your plugin's onEnable()`. No such method exists:

- A kernel plugin (`packages/core/src/types.ts`, the `Plugin` interface) has `init(ctx)`, `start?(ctx)` and `destroy?()`. It has no `onEnable`.
- `onEnable` is the app's export from `objectstack.config.ts`, which `AppPlugin` calls at boot (`skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`, the `onEnable` section; `STACK_RUNTIME_MEMBERS` in `packages/spec/src/kernel/metadata-authoring-lint.ts`).

An author who follows the comment and writes a plugin method named `onEnable` gets a method nothing calls, so the hook is never registered and nothing reports it.

## Expected

- [ ] The comment names a real seam: a plugin's `start(ctx)`, or the app's `onEnable` export. Check that the handle the example uses (`ctx.ql.registerHook`) exists on the one it names.
- [ ] The file stays at or under its token ceiling. The file sits at its ceiling, so the fix must not add bytes.

`skills/**` is Tier H.

Grade: area:ai · documentation · reach: one example comment in a published skill · evidence: read (the `Plugin` interface on `main`)
Suggested-grade: p3
Size: XS
